description:
Lists the top-level legal domains (id, domain_id, domain name). This is the first taxonomy step. It does not return subdomains, categories, documents, or jurisdictions.

When to use: When you need the domain list or a name match. Examples: 'what legal domains exist?', 'find the domain for private law'. Pass domain only to narrow by name. When not: Do not use this for children of a domain. For subdomains use list_subdomains with the returned domain_id. For categories use list_categories. For subcategories use list_subcategories. For law types use list_law_types. For documents use list_documents or search. For jurisdictions use list_jurisdictions. Skip if you already have this domain list for the same domain filter.

Parameters: domain is an optional case-insensitive substring of the domain name. There is no parent id and no iso. limit defaults to 20 and is capped at 100. next_id is the numeric id from the previous pagination.next_id; omit it on the first page. A null next_id means there is no further page. Empty data means no domain name matched.

Behavior: Read-only SELECT; does not create, update, or delete records, files, or credentials. The only effect is a database read. Auth: tools/call requires OAuth 2.0 or a Bearer token (401 if missing, invalid, revoked, or no active subscription). Rate limits: none at the MCP layer; safe to retry. Not cached; each call reads the current domain table. total_count is the full match count, not the page size. Results are not limited to a jurisdiction.

Returns: A page of {id, domain_id, domain}. Example: {"id":1,"domain_id":"A","domain":"Private law"}. Pass domain_id, not id, to list_subdomains.

next_id.description: Next ID to paginate the results

name: list_domains

data.description: Top-level domains; empty if none match. Not limited to a jurisdiction.

domain.description: Domain display name, or null when unset

domain_id.description: Domain reference, such as A. Pass this to list_subdomains as domain_id.

id.description: Numeric row id. Use only as pagination.next_id, not as domain_id.

next_id.description: Numeric id cursor for the next page, or null when there is no next page
